title: Social Expectations: East vs West
rootClaim: Eastern collectivist models of societal expectations foster greater intergenerational stability, social cohesion, and psychological resilience than Western hyper-individualism.

branches.text: Filial piety, interdependent self-construal, and family duty provide robust social safety nets and combat systemic loneliness.

children.text: Multigenerational households and communal obligation mitigate elderly isolation and insulate individuals during financial crisis.
High family pressure, rigid academic benchmarks, and filial debt generate extreme psychological burnout and youth mental health crises (e.g., Hikikomori, intense exam pressure).
Relational Harmony Model: Eastern cultural traditions prioritize emotional regulation, long-term social equilibrium, and duty over fleeting personal gratification.
Low Fertility Paradox: Extreme social and financial expectations associated with marriage and child-rearing in modern East Asian urban centers contribute to historic demographic decline.
Interdependent self-construal fosters high social trust, civic responsibility, and low violent crime rates.

branches.text: Western independent self-construal promotes personal autonomy, creative self-expression, and meritocratic self-determination.

children.text: Authenticity & Individual Agency: Western norms permit individuals to pursue careers, romantic partners, and lifestyles free from ancestral or parental coercion.
Atomization & Alienation: Extreme individualism erodes traditional civic institutions, resulting in an epidemic of loneliness, social fragmentation, and hyper-consumerism.
Elective Communities: Modern Western society allows individuals to construct intentional, interest-based social circles rather than forced obligation to birth families.

definitions.description: In Confucian philosophy, a virtue of respect for one's parents, elders, and ancestors.
A perception of the self as connected with others and defined by social roles, duties, and group harmony.
A perception of the self as an autonomous entity defined by unique internal attributes, rights, and personal choices.
A phenomenon of severe social withdrawal where individuals isolate themselves from society for extended periods.
